plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub or small tree with glossy dark green leaves and large, rose-like flowers that bloom in the cool season. It is widely cultivated in temperate gardens and prized for blooms that appear when most other plants are dormant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early spring (peak in January in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea, and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of Camellia sinensis, the plant used to make tea, and thousands of cultivars have been bred in Japan over centuries.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: A low-growing perennial with leathery evergreen leaves and nodding, cup-shaped flowers with golden stamens. It braves frost and snow, blooming in the depths of winter in woodland and shade gardens.
plants.location: Native to the mountains of central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens worldwide
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a true rose. All parts of the plant are toxic, and flowers can bloom through snow cover.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub bearing the largest flower head of any protea, with a bowl of stiff, colorful bracts surrounding a center of fuzzy florets. It thrives in the fynbos habitat of South Africa and is a popular cut flower.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with flowering often occurring from December through February in some areas
plants.location: Southwestern and southern coastal regions of South Africa
plants.funFact: The king protea is South Africa's national flower, and the protea family is so ancient that it dates back to before the supercontinent Gondwana broke apart.

plants.name: Eucalyptus leucoxylon
plants.description: A medium-sized Australian tree with smooth mottled bark and clusters of nectar-rich flowers that attract honeyeaters, lorikeets, and bees. In the Southern Hemisphere summer it provides food for countless native animals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer, with flowering occurring from autumn to winter in some forms; flowers may appear around January in some populations
plants.location: South-eastern Australia, including South Australia and Victoria
plants.funFact: Cultivated forms with deep red or pink flowers are widely planted as street trees, and the nectar is important for producing eucalyptus honey.
